title: Smoky Chipotle and Lime Chicken Fajitas with Peppers and Guacamole
summary: Chicken thigh strips marinated with chipotle, lime, cumin and smoked paprika are browned in a hot skillet, then tossed with charred peppers and onions and served with guacamole.
equipment: large cast-iron or heavy frying pan with a lid

ingredients.note: about 2 tsp zest and 2 tbsp juice

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 cm strips
red pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
yellow pepper, cut into 1 cm strips
large onion, halved and cut into 5 mm slices

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Stir the oil, lime zest and juice, chipotle, cumin, paprika, 1/4 tsp salt and the pepper together in the medium bowl. Add the chicken, toss to coat and leave for 15-30 minutes while you prepare everything else.

steps.title: Make the guacamole
steps.text: Mash the avocados with the lime juice and onion in the small bowl. No salt is needed, as the tortillas and chicken carry enough. Press cling film onto the surface to stop it browning.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in the pan over medium-high heat until just smoking. Shake the excess marinade off the chicken and cook it in 2 batches for 6-8 minutes per batch, turning, until browned and the thickest strip reaches 74 °C. Cooking in batches keeps the pan hot so the chicken browns rather than stews. Tip onto a platter and cover with foil.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the peppers and the onion to the pan, cover and cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and charred at the edges. The lid traps steam to soften them quickly. Stir in the coriander and return the chicken and its juices to the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for about 20 seconds each side and wrap them in foil. Serve the fajitas straight from the pan with the tortillas, guacamole and lime wedges.

tips: Crowding the pan is the commonest mistake; the chicken releases liquid and turns grey instead of browning.
Use a heavy cast-iron pan for the best char on the peppers.
Taste a strip before adding any salt at the table.
safety: Thighs stay juicier than breast, but check every batch reaches 74 °C.
storage: Refrigerate the chicken and vegetables within 1 hour and use within 3 days; reheat once until piping hot (74 °C). Guacamole is best eaten the same day. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
